## Exit Status

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- Every command returns an exit status
- Held on special variable `$?`
- `0`: command was successful
- `>0`: command was unsuccessful
    - Each number has specific meaning
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
echo hi
echo $?
asdf
echo $?
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
hi
0
bash: line 2: asdf: command not found
127
```


:::
:::

:::::
::::::::

## Use Exit Status

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- Special commands `&&` and `||` evaluate `$?`
- `&&` listens for exit status `0`
    - if `0` (success) then process continues
- `||` listens for exit status `>0`
    - if `>0` (fail) the process continues
- Can be combined
- Keep these simple!
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
echo hi && echo pass || echo fail
asdf && echo pass || echo fail
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
hi
pass
bash: line 1: asdf: command not found
fail
```


:::
:::

:::::
::::::::

## Square Braces

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- Square braces '`[]`' evaluate an internal statement to set exit status
- Internal exit status `0`: external exit status `0`
- Internal exit status `>0`:  external exit status `1`
- White space (spaces) is very important!
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
[ 1 == 1 ] && echo true || echo false
[ 1 == 2 ] && echo true || echo false
[ a == a ] && echo pass $? || echo fail $?
[ a == b ] && echo pass $? || echo fail $?
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
true
false
pass 0
fail 1
```


:::
:::

:::::
::::::::

## Conditionals: if

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- Conditional syntax utilize square braces for workflow control
    - i.e. execute commands only if a condition is met
- Syntax structure:
    - `if [ assertion ]`
    - New line `then`
    - Commands
    - New line `fi` to close conditional
- Conditional work only executed `if` exit status = `0`
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
if [ 1 == 1 ]; then
    echo Yay
fi
if [ 1 == 2 ]; then
    echo Nay
fi
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Yay
```


:::
:::


::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Why is `==` used and not `=`?
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::

## Conditionals: elif

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- Ability to capture workflow if first conditional fails
- `elif` (else if) assessed only when `if` exit status = `1`
- An entire new conditional is written
- Read conditionals top -> bottom
- Multiple `elif` statements allowed
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
foo=bat
if [ $foo == bar ]; then
    echo foobar
elif [ $foo == baz ]; then
    echo foobaz
elif [ $foo == bat ]; then
    echo foobat
fi
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
foobat
```


:::
:::


::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- How many conditionals failed?
- What if `foo=baz`?
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::

## Conditionals: else

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- `else` catches all failed conditions
- Specified last
- Does not evaluate an assertion
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
foo=foo
if [ $foo == bar ]; then
    echo foobar
elif [ $foo == baz ]; then
    echo foobaz
elif [ $foo == bat ]; then
    echo foobat
else
    echo "Unrecognized value of foo"
fi
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Unrecognized value of foo
```


:::
:::

:::::
::::::::

## Conditionals: and

:::::: columns
::::: {.column width="50%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 65%;"}
- Multiple assertions can be combined with `&&`
- As before, `&&` only continues if exit status = `0`
    - So, all conditionals would need to be true
::::
:::::

::::: {.column width="\"50%"}

::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
foo=bar
num=1
if [ $foo == bar ] && [ $num == 1 ]; then
    echo Success
fi
```


::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Success
```


:::
:::


::::{style="font-size: 65%;"}
::: incremental
- Would `[ $num == 1 ]` be assessed if `foo=baz`?
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::

- Keep conditionals below 3 levels of logic:
    - Simple
    - Flat
    - Short
- Consider breaking up long chains into multiple statements
- Inverting logic often simplifies

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
